# Authoring Accessibility Requirements

Adapted from the Claude accessibility-requirements guide. Use with the
[requirements template](../accessibility-requirements.md).

1. Read the concept, actual player interactions, selected platforms/inputs, and
   existing evidence. Identify barriers in visual, motor, cognitive, and auditory
   interaction. Record unknowns instead of assuming a genre, disability prevalence,
   hardware setup, or preset accessibility tier.
2. Discuss consequential scope choices with the developer. Record each selected
   commitment with an ID, affected system, expected behavior, and a feasible check.
   Existing authorization covers drafting and saving the agreed document.
3. For numerical or certification claims, verify the exact applicable requirement
   against its issuing body's current documentation. Record the source and scope;
   do not translate a general guideline into an unsupported platform obligation.
4. Trace commitments into relevant GDD, resource, interface, and framework needs.
   Later resource/UX procedures consume these IDs; their future outputs need not
   exist to author the requirements.
5. Describe human evaluation when usability or player experience is at issue.
   Inspections and automated checks support it but cannot invent the observation.
6. Save `docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md` when authorized. A blank test plan is pending
   evidence. Record actual audit scope/results when performed and revise affected
   requirements and consumers together when a decision changes.
